title: How PRINCE2 addresses people
blurb: Explain how PRINCE2 Project Management puts people at the centre of the method, and what the people element covers.
question: A new project manager says 'people are just the roles in the organization practice'. How does PRINCE2 Project Management actually address the people element?

teach.h: People sit at the centre of the method
teach.body: PRINCE2 Project Management has five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes and the project context. The people element is about the needs, capabilities and motivations of everyone involved, and the relationships between them. It covers people working on the project and people affected by it. In plain English: a project succeeds or fails through people, so the method treats them as central rather than as a box on a chart.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2, Figure 1.1; PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 4.1

head: Element
What it gives the project
rows: The setting the method is tailored to
teach.caption: People and project context were added as named elements in PRINCE2 7.

teach.h: People working on it, and people affected by it
teach.body: The organizational ecosystem is the existing set of organizations (business, users, suppliers) with their own structures, governance, culture and people. The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project. People who are affected but not in the project team still matter: they may integrate the new products into their area, so the method involves key people even when they hold no formal role.

teach.h: How the principles apply to people
head: Principle
People angle
rows: Much knowledge is hidden; use social learning
Decide at the most local level with the knowledge
Stages often bring new influencers; review how people work
Co-create products to aid adoption, cut handover risk
People factors addressed all through the lifecycle
teach.caption: PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1.

teach.body: Fernvale Housing Association is replacing its tenant repairs system using PRINCE2 Agile. Project manager Owen Achebe first maps who is affected: tenants, repair crews and call-centre staff, as well as the delivery teams. He agrees a change management approach for moving crews to the new app, a communication management approach that gathers feedback both ways, and team arrangements for a hybrid supplier team. Decisions about screen layout are left to the team, the most local level with the knowledge.

teach.text: People is not the organization practice under another name. The organization practice defines roles and responsibilities; the people element is wider: leading change, leading teams, communication and how every principle applies to people. And 'change management' here means organizational change, not change control of baselines, which belongs to the issues practice.

items: Five integrated elements: principles, people, practices, processes, project context.
People: needs, capabilities, motivations and relationships of those involved.
It covers people working on the project and people affected by it.
Four parts: leading change, leading teams, communication, people at the centre.
Each principle has a people angle, for example decisions at the most local level.
PRINCE2 Agile V2 chapter 4 builds on this: OCM, teams, communication, agile teams.

summary: You can now explain how PRINCE2 Project Management treats people as a central integrated element covering those who work on and are affected by a project. You can name the four parts of 'people central to the method' and say how the principles apply to people.

A.q: Which is one of the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management?
A.why: The five integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and the project context (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).

whyNot.0: Tailoring to the project environment was an element in the 6th edition; PRINCE2 7 uses the project context.
whyNot.1: Themes were renamed practices in PRINCE2 7.
whyNot.3: Behaviours were a PRINCE2 Agile V1 idea, now replaced by agile mindset characteristics.

A.q: Whom does the people element of PRINCE2 Project Management cover?
options: Members of the project board and the project manager
Those working on the project and those affected by it
Developers and testers inside each delivery team
Supplier staff named in the commercial management approach
A.why: People covers both those working on the project and those affected by it (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2, 3.1).

whyNot.0: Board members and the project manager are included, but the element is far wider.
whyNot.2: Delivery team members are included, but so are users and others affected by the change.
whyNot.3: Supplier staff are part of the picture, but the element is not limited to contracted roles.

A.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. In PRINCE2 Project Management, [?] are at the centre of the method, and the element covers their needs, capabilities, motivations and relationships.
A.why: People are at the centre of the method; the people element covers the needs, capabilities and motivations of those involved and the relationships between them.

whyNot.1: Products are the focus of a principle, not an element defined by needs and motivations.
whyNot.2: Processes describe the lifecycle activities, not people's needs and relationships.
whyNot.3: Practices are aspects of project management applied throughout, not the people element.

B.q: Which part of 'people central to the method' covers the change management approach, stakeholder engagement and culture?
B.why: Leading successful change covers the change management approach, stakeholder engagement and culture (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.2).

whyNot.0: Leading successful teams covers leadership, team building and social cohesion.
whyNot.1: Communication covers the communication management approach and two-way information flow.
whyNot.2: Tailoring to the project context is what the 'tailor to suit the project' principle does; it is not one of the four people parts.

B.q:
Which two statements about the people element are correct?
1. People is one of the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management.
2. People is the new name for the organization practice.
3. It covers those affected by the project as well as those working on it.
4. It was one of the four elements of the 6th edition.
B.why: People is one of the five integrated elements, and it covers both those working on and those affected by the project.

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: the organization practice still exists and defines roles; people is a wider element.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: people is not the organization practice, and the 6th edition elements were principles, themes, processes and tailoring.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: people became a named element in PRINCE2 7.

B.q: How does the 'manage by exception' principle apply to people?
options: Decisions are taken at the most local level that has the knowledge
Decisions are referred upward to the project board for approval
Decisions sit with the project manager to keep them consistent across teams
Decisions wait for the next stage boundary to be reviewed
B.why: Decisions should be made at the most local level where the knowledge to make and own them resides, escalating when they could affect other areas (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.1: Referring routine decisions upward is the opposite of managing by exception.
whyNot.2: Centralizing decisions with the project manager ignores where the knowledge sits.
whyNot.3: Holding decisions for stage boundaries would slow delivery; local decisions are made as needed.

C.q: Which pairing correctly links a part of 'people central to the method' with the management approach that supports it?
options: Leading successful teams: communication management approach
Leading successful change: change management approach
Leading successful change: issue management approach
C.why: Leading successful change is supported by the change management approach, which describes moving from the current to the target state.

whyNot.0: The communication management approach supports the communication part, not leading teams.
whyNot.1: The quality management approach belongs to the quality practice.
whyNot.3: The issue management approach handles change control of baselines, not organizational change.

C.q: How does the 'focus on products' principle apply to people?
options: Products are specified in full before users are involved
Co-creating products with users improves adoption
Product descriptions remove the need for stakeholder input
Users first see the products at the project closure workshop
C.why: Co-creating products with business, user and supplier communities unites perspectives, improves adoption and reduces handover risks (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.0: Specifying everything before involving users loses the adoption benefits of co-creation.
whyNot.2: Product descriptions are agreed with stakeholders, not used to avoid them.
whyNot.3: Users are involved throughout through co-creation and demos, not just at closure.

C.q: A project manager says people issues are fully covered by the organization practice. Which is the BEST response?
options: The organization practice also holds the change management approach
People matters are handled in the issues practice through change control
The quality practice covers communication with affected users
People is a separate element covering change, teams and communication
C.why: People is one of the five integrated elements, covering leading successful change, leading successful teams, communication and how the principles apply to people.

whyNot.0: The change management approach belongs to the people element, not the organization practice.
whyNot.1: Change control of baselines is about issues, not about people and organizational change.
whyNot.2: Communication is part of the people element through the communication management approach.

reteach.title: A new kitchen nobody cooks in
reteach.question: If a canteen gets a brand-new kitchen but the cooks were never asked, trained or listened to, has the project succeeded?

blocks.body: A shiny kitchen is an output. It only creates value when cooks change how they work. That is why PRINCE2 Project Management puts people at the centre: the people building the kitchen and the cooks who will use it both shape success. Leading the change, leading the team, and talking (and listening) to everyone are part of the method, not extras.

blocks.h: Four parts of the people element

blocks.text: The organization practice gives roles; the people element asks how those people, and everyone affected, will actually work together and adopt the change.

explain.body: PRINCE2 Project Management integrates principles, people, practices, processes and the project context. Principles are the foundation; people sit at the centre.

test.q: Which list gives the five integrated elements of PRINCE2 Project Management?
options: Principles, people, practices, processes, project context
Principles, practices, roles, processes, project environment
test.why: The five integrated elements are principles, people, practices, processes and the project context (PRINCE2 7 manual 1.2).

whyNot.0: Themes and tailoring belong to the 6th edition's four elements.
whyNot.1: Products are a principle's focus, not an element; project context is missing.
whyNot.3: Roles belong to the organization practice, and project environment is the older 6th edition wording.

explain.body: The organizational ecosystem is the existing business, users and suppliers. The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project.

rows.label: Made of
values: People and ways of working for the project

test.q: The temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for a project is the:
test.why: The project ecosystem is the temporary set of people, relationships, structures and ways of working created for the project (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.1).

whyNot.0: The organizational ecosystem is the existing organizations, not the temporary project one.
whyNot.2: The project management team is the set of management roles, not the whole ecosystem.
whyNot.3: A delivery team builds products; the ecosystem is much wider.

explain.body: PRINCE2 7 groups its people guidance into four parts: leading successful change, leading successful teams, communication, and people at the centre of the method.

test.q: Which is one of the four parts of 'people central to the method'?
test.why: The four parts are leading successful change, leading successful teams, communication, and people at the centre.

whyNot.0: Managing product delivery is a process.
whyNot.1: Agile enablement is the name of a workshop in directing a project.
whyNot.2: Benefits realization belongs to the business case practice.

explain.body: Much valuable knowledge is hidden in the project ecosystem. Behaviours, culture and relationships are hard to write down, so they are best learned through social learning in a collaborative, knowledge-sharing environment.

test.q: Why does PRINCE2 Project Management stress social learning for people-related lessons?
options: Behaviours and relationships are hard to capture in documents
Lessons logs are not kept as part of the project log in agile projects
Project assurance can review spoken lessons faster than written ones
The board approves written lessons at the closure workshop
test.why: Behaviours, culture and relationships are hard to document, so they are best learned socially (PRINCE2 7 manual 3.5.1).

whyNot.1: The lessons log is still part of the project log in PRINCE2 Agile.
whyNot.2: Project assurance speed is not the reason given.
whyNot.3: Board approval of written lessons is not why social learning is stressed.
